places.name: The Distilleries
places.epithet: Where foreign cargo is made respectable
places.text: Resins, spices, oils and aromatics landed in Caer Veyn come up here to be distilled and blended into the perfumes Marlmond is famous for.
places.source: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

places.name: The Bottling-Houses
places.epithet: The reason the customs law runs to eleven pages
places.text: Where foreign goods are rebottled in Marlmond glass and relabelled as Crownweave goods. Anything that smells of Stormwake in The Crown's markets probably passed through here on the way.
places.source: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

places.name: The Marlmond Glasshouse
places.text: The furnaces that blow the town's own bottles: thin, faintly violet, and stamped on the base with a mark that customs clerks have learned to trust a little too much.

places.name: The Customs House
places.text: Where the Union tries to keep track of what goes into Marlmond's vats as foreign and comes out as domestic. The clerks are thorough; the bottlers are more so.
places.source: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

places.name: The Label House
places.text: Printers and calligraphers who make the labels, in the right ink, the right hand and the right language for whichever market a bottle is going to.

places.name: Blending Square
places.text: The market square, which smells of everything at once.

places.name: The Still Lanes
places.text: Streets of small family stills, each with a recipe it will not share and a neighbour it suspects of stealing it.

places.name: The Newbomyard Trail
places.source: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East
